name: Som-Raychaudhuri Rotating Universe
description: A homogeneous universe of charged dust in rigid rotation, held in a uniform magnetic field along the axis of rotation. Its line element is the shortest of Gödel's kind, and the circles about any world line of the dust are closed timelike curves beyond $r = c/\Omega$.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and $\Omega$ is the angular velocity of the dust, so $c/\Omega$ is the one length of the solution. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Fill all of space with dust, give every grain an electric charge, and set the whole cloud turning rigidly about an axis. What does gravity make of it? Murari Mohan Som finished his doctorate under Amal Kumar Raychaudhuri in Calcutta in 1967, and in 1968 the two of them put that question to the Einstein-Maxwell equations [mathgenealogysom, som1968]. Willem Jacob van Stockum had solved the same problem for dust without charge in 1937 [vanstockum1937]. With charge, Som and Raychaudhuri found a family of solutions in which the Lorentz force on the dust vanishes everywhere and the ratio of charge density to mass density may take any value, and they remarked that these solutions "do not seem to have any classical analogue" [som1968].¶One member of the family is about as simple as a rotating universe gets: its dust has the same density of mass and of charge everywhere, and its line element is that of flat space with $\Omega r^2d\phi/c$ added to $c\,dt$, where $\Omega$ is the rate of rotation [paiva2011]. Stand on any grain and look outward: the circle around you at $r = c/\Omega$ is null, so light led around it by mirrors arrives back at the moment it left, and every circle beyond it is a closed timelike curve, a path a rocket can follow back to the very event it started from [drukker2004]. The universe is the same at every event, so every grain of the dust sits at the center of such a circle [reboucas1983].¶Kurt Gödel's universe of 1949 is rotating dust too, with closed timelike curves through every event [godel1949]. The first step toward relating the two was Raychaudhuri's own: with S. N. Guha Thakurta he worked out, in 1980, a condition that a metric of Gödel's kind must satisfy to be homogeneous [raychaudhuri1980]. Three years later, in Rio de Janeiro, Marcelo Rebouças and Jayme Tiomno proved that the condition is also sufficient, and that two numbers label every such universe: the vorticity $\Omega$ and a second parameter $m$ [reboucas1983]. Gödel's universe has $m^2 = 2\Omega^2$ and Som and Raychaudhuri's has $m = 0$, and at $m^2 = 4\Omega^2$ Rebouças and Tiomno found "a completely causal space-time-homogeneous rotating universe" [reboucas1983, boyda2003].¶Can a traveler here really reach the past? By 1975 Som was supervising a doctorate in Rio de Janeiro, Antonio Teixeira's [mathgenealogysom], and in 1987 Teixeira, Rebouças, and F. M. Paiva studied the geodesics and the causality of what they called the homogeneous Som-Raychaudhuri universe [paiva1987]. Every body in free fall moves on a helix about some line parallel to the axis, which is a circle seen from above: light crossing the axis at right angles circles at radius $c/2\Omega$, and matter circles closer in [paiva2011]. So light sent out from a grain never gets farther from it than $c/\Omega$, and no geodesic returns to its own past [paiva2011, drukker2004]. The trip takes a rocket: circle opposite to the rotation at radius $r$ and speed $V$ with $Vr > c^2/\Omega$, and each lap ends before it began [paiva2011].¶String theory arrived at the same universe from another direction: Gary Horowitz and Arkady Tseytlin, hunting for exact solutions, wrote down the spacetime of a uniform magnetic field and noted that it "describes a rotating universe": the line element is Som and Raychaudhuri's [horowitz1995]. Jorge Russo and Tseytlin then solved for the spectrum of a closed string moving in it [russo1995]. Jerome Gauntlett, Jan Gutowski, Christopher Hull, Stathis Pakis, and Harvey Reall found a supersymmetric universe of Gödel's kind in five dimensions [gauntlett2003], and Edward Boyda, Surya Ganguli, Petr Hořava, and Uday Varadarajan observed that Som and Raychaudhuri's metric is "a closer analog of the string theory Gödel universe than Gödel's solution itself" [boyda2003].¶Why would nobody inside see the trouble? Boyda and his collaborators answered with holography: the screen that bounds what an observer riding the dust can see is a surface of finite size around her, and the closed timelike curves are "either hidden behind the holographic screen, or broken by it into causal pieces" [boyda2003]. Nadav Drukker, Bartomeu Fiol, and Joan Simón, and independently Yasuaki Hikida and Soo-Jong Rey, recognized an old friend in the motion: a particle here moves as an electron does in a uniform magnetic field, on Larmor circles, with Landau levels for its quantum states [drukker2004, hikida2003]. Drukker, Fiol, and Simón also showed that in the supergravity versions of this universe a supertube wrapped around a closed timelike curve has modes with negative kinetic terms, and they built a wall of supertubes around a region that looks like the same universe inside and holds no closed timelike curve [drukker2003].

related.text: Kurt Gödel's rotating dust of 1949, homogeneous as this universe is. Marcelo Rebouças and Jayme Tiomno's family of homogeneous rotating universes holds both, Gödel's at $m^2 = 2\Omega^2$ and this one at $m = 0$ [godel1949, reboucas1983].
Willem Jacob van Stockum's cylinder of rotating dust without charge. Its line element is this one's with $R = c/\Omega$ and a factor $e^{-r^2/R^2}$ on $dr^2 + dz^2$ [vanstockum1937].

A spinning string adds the constant $a\,d\phi$ to $c\,dt$ where this universe adds $\Omega r^2d\phi/c$. Harald Soleng's frame for a string of finite thickness, $(c\,dt + M\,d\phi)^2$ with $M(r)$ free, is this universe at $M = \Omega r^2/c$ with circles of circumference $2\pi r$, where his heat flow vanishes [soleng1994].
The dust at rest, $\Omega = 0$, where the density vanishes and the line element is flat space in cylindrical coordinates.
Uncharged dust that turns faster near its axis than far from it, with no magnetic field to help. Its circles about the axis stay spacelike at every radius [maitra1966, chan2024].

coordinates.name: Cylindrical
domains: r = c/\Omega \;\text{(the circle of constant } t, r, z \text{ is null)}
r > c/\Omega \;\text{(the circles of constant } t, r, z \text{ are closed timelike curves)}

parameters.description: Angular velocity of the dust, the vorticity of its world lines; the circle of constant $t$, $r$, and $z$ is null at $r = c/\Omega$

coordinates.convention: We use Som and Raychaudhuri's cylindrical coordinates $(t, r, \phi, z)$ about one world line of the dust, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $r$ the proper distance from that world line, and $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Cartesian

parameters.description: Angular velocity of the dust, the vorticity of its world lines

coordinates.convention: We use the Cartesian coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$ of Drukker, Fiol, and Simón, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $x = r\cos\phi$, and $y = r\sin\phi$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
